strongest_counterhypothesis: A conventional path — preserve module boundaries during validation, use a purpose-built protected regression/lesion/replay suite, apply ordinary compiler optimization, and make fusion decisions manually — can match CQC defect coverage and safety with less compiler/meta-architecture complexity.
synthetic_adjudication: The current synthetic discriminator does not test developer effort, maintainability, real compiler complexity, stochastic state abstraction, or real Frank fault coverage. It therefore cannot defeat the conventional baseline.
why_cqc_still_survives: The synthetic model demonstrates a real failure class for output-only/normal-only equivalence and shows that an explicit intervention-scoped quotient can compress exact duplicates without those modeled causal errors. It justifies a real matched test, not promotion.
kill_rule: REFUTE CQC if a conventional regression/compiler/manual-fusion baseline matches protected fault detection, replay/recovery parity and reproducibility on real Frank component baselines while using materially less implementation complexity/resources.
promotion_rule: Only consider promotion if CQC adds measurable defect coverage, reduces architecture/test maintenance, or reduces runtime/resource/search complexity without critical correctness/recovery/authority regression on accepted-target evidence.
